why: Fails all three checks. (1) CITATION. The quoted sentence does not exist on the cited page: the word 'timeout' occurs ZERO times in all 306 lines of agent-sdk/session-storage.md (grep -aic 'timeout' = 0; 'per-call' = 0). It is verbatim on agent-sdk/python.md:868, a ClaudeAgentOptions field row, with a differently-worded TypeScript twin at agent-sdk/typescript.md:431 marked '*Alpha.*'. The finding self-discloses this, but a finding filed under slug agent-sdk/session-storage whose contract sentence lives on another page is the citation failure the protocol treats as refuting outright. session-storage.md imposes no timeout requirement of any kind. (2) WRONG SUBSYSTEM. typescript.md:431 reads: 'Timeout in milliseconds for each `sessionStore.load()` and `sessionStore.listSubkeys()` call during resume materialization. If the adapter doesn't settle within this window, the query fails instead of hanging. Ignored when `sessionStore` is not set.' That bounds the SDK calling ARBITRARY USER-SUPPLIED adapter code (S3/Redis/Postgres over the network) and its documented outcome is to FAIL THE QUERY. packages/shared/src/sessions/mirror/ is not that surface. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-session-mirror-store.md:7 records the owner decision in the plan header: 'No shipped runtime consumes Claude's SDK option - the page is a design template, so the interface shape is portability guidance, not a compatibility surface', and the names were deliberately changed to SessionMirrorStore/MirrorSessionKey to avoid colliding with the local store-v2 SessionStore. There is exactly ONE adapter: config/session-mirror-settings.ts:37-38 throws 'unknown session mirror adapter' for any name but 'directory' (host.ts:76-78 carries the same note), so the pluggable-network-backend hazard class the bound exists for cannot be configured in this fork. (3) CONTRACT INVERSION. The documented behaviour on timeout is that the query FAILS. Our restore is deliberately the opposite and says so at restore.ts:76 and :90 - 'Never throws - a broken mirror must not break session open' - returning false. Adopting the documented bound verbatim would make a mirror stall fail session open, reversing a shipped intentional deviation. (4) THE list_subkeys HALF IS A DATED OWNER DECISION. 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 item 8: 'MirrorSessionKey.subpath + SessionMirrorStore.listSubkeys - 2026-07-28-session-mirror-store.md, Task 4: subagent-transcript restore via listSubkeys is contract-ready in the adapters but has no host producer yet - the queue mirrors only the main session JSONL today ... (exactly the documented consequence of the missing half).' restore.ts never calls listSubkeys, so half the claimed behaviour has no call to bound, by recorded decision. (5) CONSEQUENCE OVERSTATED ON ITS OWN FACTS. The identifier claim is literally true - restore.ts:129 is a bare `await store.load(...)` and SessionManager.ts:7573 awaits restoreMissingMirroredSessions inside initialize() before initGate.markReady(), so a stall there would block IPC. But the claimed remedy does not deliver the claimed benefit for the claimed scenario: the only adapter reads via fs/promises.readFile (directory.ts:74) on a filesystem path, and on a hung NFS/SMB mount that pins a libuv threadpool thread in an uninterruptible kernel wait - a Promise.race would resolve the JS promise while the thread stays pinned, and with UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE=4 every other fs op in the process stalls regardless. Blast radius is also narrower than stated: restore.ts:98 returns immediately when no sessionMirror is configured (the default, 'absent config = no mirror, zero overhead'), and restore.ts:111 skips every session whose local jsonl is present and readable, so the normal boot performs zero mirror reads.
correctedState: Accurate as an identifier observation, wrong as a doc divergence. agent-sdk/session-storage.md contains no timeout requirement (0 occurrences of 'timeout'); the quoted sentence is the Python SDK's ClaudeAgentOptions.load_timeout_ms row (python.md:868), whose TypeScript twin loadTimeoutMs is marked '*Alpha.*' (typescript.md:431) and bounds the SDK's calls into a USER-SUPPLIED SessionStore adapter, failing the query on expiry. Nessy has no such pluggable surface: session-mirror-settings.ts:37-38 fails closed on any adapter but 'directory', and the plan header (2026-07-28-session-mirror-store.md:7) records that the SDK interface is 'portability guidance, not a compatibility surface'. Our restore contract is deliberately the inverse of the documented one - 'Never throws - a broken mirror must not break session open' (restore.ts:76). The list_subkeys half is inapplicable by dated owner decision (inert-worklist section 3 item 8: listSubkeys is contract-ready in the adapters with no host producer). What remains is a narrow, opt-in-only robustness note, not a parity gap: with sessionMirror configured on a stalling mount, the pre-listing sweep awaited in SessionManager.initialize():7573 could block startup - though a JS-level Promise.race would not actually unblock it, since the hang is an uninterruptible fs read pinning a libuv threadpool thread, not a slow in-JS network call.
